features.name: Manager views their team's pending requests
Manager approves or rejects a request
Employee views their own leave balance

assumptions.statement: Every employee has exactly one manager, identified by manager_id; the brief gives no org-chart detail beyond "a company of 200 employees", so a flat one-level approval chain is assumed rather than multi-level escalation.
Each employee gets a fixed annual allotment of 20 paid leave days, decremented on approval, not on request — a rejected or pending request never touches the balance.
A request cannot be approved if it would take the balance negative; the API returns 409 rather than silently allowing an overdraw.
Authentication is a bearer token whose payload carries the employee_id and role (employee|manager); the brief specifies no auth mechanism.

business_rules: BR-01: Every endpoint requires a valid bearer token; missing or invalid returns 401.
BR-02: An employee can only see and act on their own requests; a manager can additionally see requests where they are the named manager_id.
BR-03: A leave request needs a start_date, end_date, and reason; end_date before start_date is 422.
BR-04: Only a pending request can be approved or rejected; acting on an already-decided request returns 409.
BR-05: Approving a request that would exceed the remaining balance returns 409 and does not decrement anything.
BR-06: A manager cannot approve or reject their own request, even if it happens to route through their own manager_id by data error — checked explicitly, not assumed impossible.

collections.name: employees
fields: email string required unique lowercase indexed

collections.name: leave_requests
fields: status string required enum(pending,approved,rejected) default pending indexed

request.status: query param, optional, filters to pending|approved|rejected

response.items: array of leave_requests scoped to caller (BR-02)
